name: Hrádecký dub

location.address: Beside the Hrádecký mill pond (Hrádecký mlýnský rybník), Hrádek u Sušice, Klatovy District, Plzeň Region
location.neighbourhood: Hrádek u Sušice, about 4km from Sušice

access: Free, open public ground on the bank of the mill pond; no gate or ticket
transport: In Hrádek u Sušice village, about 4km from Sušice; no public transport reaches the pond directly, reachable on foot or by road from the village
verify_notes: Two independent sources beyond the AOPK CR Pamatne stromy register (kod 102466, girth 411cm in our register snapshot, no age field): cs.wikipedia.org dedicated article (cites the same registry number 102466/9266, but adds its own detail: girth 485cm measured 2012, height 28m, crown width 20m, age estimated 440 years, protected since 1978, elevation 475m, coordinates 49.15'42.6"N 13.29'42.8"E which resolve close to our pin) and turistika.cz (independent Czech tourism site, last updated 2021-05-07, describes it as "a truly massive tree in good condition" with photos showing it alive and standing, gives its own age estimate of roughly 400 years, coordinates 49.261,13.499). GIRTH CONFLICT, flagged: our register snapshot gives 411cm; Wikipedia states 485cm from a 2012 AOPK measurement under the same registry number. Both cannot be right for the same measurement date; recorded girth_cm as our own register figure since that is the field this project holds directly, but the writer should treat the exact number as uncertain and could round it ("over four metres round") rather than quote either figure as precise. AGE: two sources roughly agree, 400 (turistika, undated basis) and 440 (Wikipedia/AOPK, undated basis) years; neither states how the age was derived (not stated as girth-derived), so both are source estimates rather than our own derivation. Two neighbouring memorial trees noted nearby in the Wikipedia article (Hrádecká lípa, Lešišovská lípa) -- worth a look for a future pass in this same village, though not researched this pass. Grows near a working millpond, a genuinely public spot with no access barrier found in either source. DESTINATION TEST: does not clearly clear it alone. A genuinely old (400+ year), protected, publicly accessible oak with real photographs, but no legend, event or superlative found in either source beyond the registration itself; nearest published tree is 26.4km away (Zwieslerwaldhaus), beyond a comfortable day-trip radius and with no direct public transport. The Wikipedia article names two more protected trees in the same village (Hrádecká lípa, Lešišovská lípa) not researched this pass; if those verify, Hrádek u Sušice could cluster to 3 trees, still short of the ordinary 4-tree floor but a stronger case than one tree alone. Recommend HOLD pending that check rather than shipping as a single-famous-tree exception on a modest record.

name: Buk u rybníčku

location.address: By a former pond on the edge of the village, Nová Ves pod Pleší, Příbram District, Central Bohemian Region
location.neighbourhood: Nová Ves pod Pleší, about 9km from Dobříš

access: Free, on open ground by a pond at the edge of the village; no gate or ticket found in any source
transport: Nová Ves pod Pleší village, Příbram District; about 9km from Dobříš, roughly 40km southwest of Prague; no direct public transport to the pond itself
verify_notes: The lead photo filenames reference nova_ves_pod_plesi; CONFIRMED as the same village as the register coordinate (49.841,14.269), resolving the open question in the leads file. Register: AOPK CR Pamatne stromy, kod 103427, girth 308cm (matches exactly, no conflict). Independent existence confirmation beyond the register/Wikipedia mirror: nasedobrissko.cz (NASÉ Dobrissko, a regional heritage site, unrelated publisher) names it directly as one of the village's two memorial trees, "o nichz uz vznikaly pribehy" (stories have already grown up around it); mistopisy.cz (a separate tourism/gazetteer site) independently places a protected forest beech "near the pond on the right side outside the village", matching the register location. Official ISOP Portal page (portal.nature.cz/w/uzemi-7463, itself an AOPK CR page, so same source as the register) gives the designation date as 2004-09-21. Czech Wikipedia's district-list mirror of the same AOPK record (raw wikitext, Pstrom template ids 10227/103427/Q26788530, exact coordinate and girth match) adds health notes not present in our register snapshot: in 2004 an open cavity in the trunk was noted, otherwise undamaged, 5% crown dieback, normal foliage; in 2019 a large branch broke off leaving a big wound, with rot visible and fruiting bodies of Fomes fomentarius (a decay fungus) at the crown base, plus a smaller cavity used for nesting. This is useful ALIVE evidence as recently as 2019 and explains why the tree reads as a genuine veteran despite a modest 308cm girth (forest-grown, declining). NO SOURCE anywhere gives a numeric age; a search-engine AI summary claimed "more than 150 years" but this could not be confirmed on any directly fetched page, so per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule it is NOT used and age_estimate is left as not documented. A future pass could derive an age from the girth with a cited beech growth-rate figure; not done this pass for lack of time to find a properly citable rate. DESTINATION TEST: does not clear it alone. A modest 308cm forest beech, no documented age, its distinguishing fact is decline (a 2019 storm wound, fungal fruiting bodies, a nesting cavity) rather than scale or legend; nearest published tree is 25.7km away (Prague), beyond the day-trip boundary with no direct transport to the pond. Recommend HOLD; same shape as the Belgium leads held the same week for an identical reason (thin single tree, no cluster, modest fame).
